item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-28: reverse-function
item.description:
# Reverse-a-function drill — 2026-11-28
Target: Windows x86-64 (unsigned arg in `ecx`; return in `eax`).
Reverse this function to equivalent C. Two new things here: `shr` drops a bit into the carry flag, and `adc` ("add with carry") adds that flag back in.
```asm mystery: mov eax, ecx shr eax, 1 ; CF = the bit shifted out (old bit 0) adc eax, 0 ; eax = eax + 0 + CF ret ```
What does it return for 7, 8 and 0xFFFFFFFF?
---
## Answer
```c unsigned mystery(unsigned x) { return (x >> 1) + (x & 1); // x / 2, rounding halves up } ```
Results: 4, 4 and 0x80000000.
## Explanation
- The last bit a shift pushes out lands in CF. For `shr eax, 1` that's the old bit 0, so CF = 1 exactly when x is odd. - `adc eax, 0` adds nothing except the carry, so odd inputs get +1: 7 → 3 + 1 = 4, 8 → 4 + 0 = 4. - It's the same as `(x + 1) / 2` but can't overflow. For 0xFFFFFFFF, `x + 1` wraps to 0, while this gives 0x7FFFFFFF + 1 = 0x80000000.
